Windows one-file release of VBA Add-in Editor. The ZIP contains `VBAAddinEditor.exe` and its SHA-256 checksum file.

## Every file opens and stays editable

The editor's password-protection detection reported legitimate add-ins as password-protected and made them read-only. The check tried to decode the VBA project's protection metadata and treated anything unusual as protected, so healthy files were blocked. That detection — the read-only banner, the save block, the import block and the module-edit warnings built on it — is gone.

- Files the editor used to call "password-protected" now open and edit like any other: VBA modules, the ribbon designer, the Package XML view, ports from another add-in.
- The protection records inside the VBA project (`CMG`/`DPB`/`GC`) are never rewritten: a save copies them through verbatim, the same way pyOpenVBA preserves them.
- Verified against add-ins carrying real protection records: the project password stays set, the records stay byte-identical, and module edits save and reopen correctly.
- Opening the project's password in the VBA editor still works as before; the editor never reads, checks or removes the password itself.

An authentication layer is planned for a future version. Until then, treat the editor's write access the way you treat the VBA editor's: keep the automatic backup on.

## Notes

- This is a development build, built and tested on GitHub's Windows runner. It has not been through the live Excel/PowerPoint qualification matrix. Keep the automatic backup on.
- Known bug: a module whose code starts with a blank line fails save verification ("Body mismatch"). The original file is left untouched; remove the leading blank line and save again.
